items.title: CoinDCX's Admission Contradicts Prior Leadership Claims
points: CoinDCX's CEO had previously publicly dismissed or denied specific losses that the exchange has now admitted were real.
The reversal suggests either a material change in the exchange's financial position or a prior misrepresentation of facts to stakeholders.
Timing and exact nature of the reversal remain unclear, but the contradiction directly damages investor and user confidence in management credibility amid heightened scrutiny of crypto exchanges.

items.title: a16z Crypto Becomes a16z Frontier
points: a16z Crypto has rebranded as a16z Frontier to invest beyond blockchain in AI-native apps, autonomous machines, and biomedical systems.

Rationale: broad blockchain adoption has blurred the line between crypto-native and conventional companies, making a vertical-specific fund label imprecise; stablecoins (crypto tokens pegged to a stable asset like the US dollar) are cited as payment rails for machine-to-machine networks.
The rebrand coincides with the departure of a founding member from the firm.

items.title: Argentine Judge Dismisses LIBRA Token Case Against Milei
points: An Argentine judge dismissed the criminal case against President Milei and 10 others over the LIBRA token, ruling that promoting a token is not inherently fraudulent.
This comes despite $107M in cashouts from team-controlled wallets.

items.title: Bitcoin Price Resistance and Liquidation Cascade
points: Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000, triggering $404M in long liquidations (forced closures of leveraged bets that price would rise) in four hours and $815M total over 24 hours, affecting 201,012 traders.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that hold Bitcoin directly) still saw $304.73M in net weekly inflows despite the dip.

The $87,000–$87,700 zone is identified as key resistance, where holders of 6–12 month-old coins sit near their cost basis and tend to sell into rallies; the 2026 opening price ($87,490) and 20-month moving average ($87,165) reinforce this ceiling.
Below spot, $80,000–$81,500 offers overlapping support, anchored by the US spot Bitcoin ETF holders' average cost basis ($81,500) and concentrated buy orders at $80,000.

items.title: SEC Tokenization Exemption Clarity Gap
points: The SEC's new tokenization exemption hinges on a blockchain being 'public and permissionless,' but this definition remains ambiguous.
Canton Network (a private, permissioned chain used by Goldman Sachs) and Ethereum layer-2s (scaling networks built on top of Ethereum) with centralized sequencers sit in unclear territory.

Only chains meeting the permissionless threshold benefit from the exemption, pressuring the SEC for definitive guidance, and it remains unresolved whether companies can have their equity tokenized without consent under the current framing.

items.title: Phantom Rolls Out Kalshi Prediction Markets
points: Kalshi event contracts (bets on real-world event outcomes) expanded to US users via Phantom wallet starting October 23, with access rolling out over coming weeks.

Users complete identity verification (KYC) on Kalshi and fund trades with Phantom's CASH stablecoin; Phantom charges $0.02 per contract feed fee plus a network fee, with winnings returned to Phantom Cash accounts.
Phantom's General Counsel says CFTC jurisdiction is clear under its no-action position but expects the matter to eventually reach the Supreme Court.
Certain markets are blocked state-by-state: sports in Michigan; sports, elections, politics, and entertainment in Nevada; and a longer list of restrictions in Washington.

items.title: Hash-Only Rollup Replaces ECDSA Signatures
points: A bb84 Payments founder deployed an OP Stack layer-2 (chain ID 42069000, live since September 30) that uses Lamport-style keccak-256 hash chains instead of ECDSA signatures (the standard cryptographic method for authorizing blockchain transactions) for transactions.
Each account derives from a secret seed generating a 1,000-step hash chain tracked by a NullifierTree predeploy, using two new transaction types for commit and reveal steps.

The chain targets roughly a 2^128 quantum work factor (resistance to being broken by quantum computers running Grover's algorithm) inside the L2, but ECDSA remains at the L1 boundary, fault proofs are absent, the sequencer is centralized, and stateful wallets risk lockout if chain position is lost.

items.title: Robinhood Stock Tokens Enable Collateralized Lending
points: Morpho launched credit markets for Robinhood Stock Tokens, letting users post tokenized equities as collateral to borrow stablecoins on-chain.
The system uses a two-layer architecture: Robinhood Chain handles tokenization while Morpho runs the credit network, letting any app integrate stock-backed lending without custom infrastructure.
